entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Flavius Appalius Illus Trocundes was a prominent general of the Eastern Roman Empire, whose involvement in the rise and fall of Emperor Basiliscus and the rebellion against Emperor Zeno significantly impacted the trajectory of the empire during the late 5th century CE.



Trocundes played a crucial role in the Basilican Schism, a period of civil war that ravaged the empire, and his leadership during the rebellion against Emperor Zeno is believed to have contributed to the eventual collapse of the Western Roman Empire. His actions had far-reaching consequences, shaping the course of Eastern Roman history and influencing the subsequent rise of the Byzantine Empire.




This pivotal figure's legacy continues to be studied by historians, offering valuable insights into the complexities of late antiquity and the dynamics of imperial power.




The story of Flavius Appalius Illus Trocundes serves as a testament to the enduring impact of historical figures on the shaping of human civilization, their influence still felt centuries after their passing.
